newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil slips as support wanes.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil slips as support wanes.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps slipped slightly late afternoon on Thursday on ample physical offers amid waning buying support from some traders, industry sources said on Thursday.
June gas oil swaps were last quoted at $24.80/$24.90 per barrel down 10 cents from Wednesday while July was seen at $24.65/$24.75, also down 10 cents.
Traders said the market is under some pressure over worries about unsold prompt supplies in the physical market of 150,000 tonnes.
Also the lower award by Taiwan state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp of two 225,000-250,000 barrel cargoes at around $24.60 per barrel on a free-on-board basis has raised some concern.
Traders said this could be the first time cargoes have been sold by a regular exporter at below the $25.00 per barrel mark.
In addition to the supply surplus, the reduced buying power of some traders has also raised some concerns.

The group of local traders who since March 3 bought well over 19 million barrels are slowing down their purchases. In the past the traders have bought up to 2.44 million barrels in one day compared to the recent average purchases of about 300,000
Fuel oil was last quoted at $101.25/$102.50, also little moved from Wednesday quotes.
